extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners designing or evaluating LLM benchmarks for mathematical reasoning
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating benchmarks (RV-Bench) that test large language models' genuine mathematical reasoning by generating 'unseen' random-variable variants of existing problems and measuring models' accuracy and robustness across variable combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use question-generating functions to produce RVQs
rubrics_metrics.description: Build question-generating functions to produce random variable questions (RVQs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RVQs are generated so that their background content mirrors original benchmark problems, but with randomized variable combinations. The generation mechanism should produce diverse variable combinations so that instances are 'unseen' to LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background content should mirror original problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The RVQs' background content should mirror the original benchmark problems' background content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping background content similar preserves the underlying problem pattern while randomizing variables, ensuring that success requires understanding the underlying reasoning rather than memorizing surface forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomize variable combinations to create 'unseen' instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized variable combinations render RVQs 'unseen' to LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The randomized combinations must be sufficiently varied so that models cannot rely on memorized training items but must generalize the problem pattern to answer correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate models on accuracy and robustness on RV-Bench
rubrics_metrics.description: An LLM's genuine reasoning capability is reflected through its accuracy and robustness on RV-Bench.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accuracy (correctness over RVQs) and robustness (performance stability across diverse variable combinations) as primary evaluation metrics to quantify reasoning ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare performance on encountered vs. 'unseen' distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess proficiency imbalance between encountered (original) and 'unseen' (RVQ) data distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report differences in model performance between standard benchmark instances and the RV-generated unseen variants to reveal overfitting or lack of generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure generalization across similar mathematical reasoning tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how well proficiency generalizes across similar mathematical reasoning tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that generalization is often limited; include cross-task evaluations to determine transfer behavior and report limitations explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use test-time scaling to elicit generalization when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Test-time scaling can be used to effectively elicit proficiency generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a methodological option, apply test-time scaling techniques during evaluation and report their effect on RVQ performance as a way to probe latent generalization capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design benchmarks to avoid simplistic design and data contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A reliable benchmark should address issues such as simplistic design and potential data contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure benchmark instances are non-trivial and verify that evaluation data are not present in model training corpora to avoid inflated performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale experiments across many models and RVQs
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct extensive experiments across a diverse set of models and many RVQs to validate findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports experiments on over 30 representative LLMs across more than 1,000 RVQs; similar scale is recommended to robustly characterize model behavior.
